correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=3, B>0 and t>0, joint convexity of Thomson flow energy yields global symmetrization without an a-priori symmetric design restriction. Series/parallel reduction after any one edge failure gives exactly the two rational objective branches. Their difference is (r-1)[1/r-2/((m-1)(m-2+r))], with strictly positive bracket. Derivative numerators t[(m-2+r)^2+2(m-2)]-2(m-1) and -(m-1)/r^2+2t/(m-1) have unique zeros, deriving both closed-form thresholds and the joining regime. Boundary cases r=1 and positive t are included. Standalone verify.py independently checks the identities and matrix computations. No uniqueness among arbitrary asymmetric optimizers is claimed.

value.rationale: An m-route two-terminal hub network is a canonical multiply redundant series-parallel graph, and worst failed-edge endpoint resistance measures the cost of routing around any failed wire. A single specially priced route is the minimal heterogeneous price perturbation of this symmetric family. The exact all-size allocation and broad plateau t_-(m)<=t<=t_+(m), with width t_+/t_- asymptotic to m^3/4, capture a nontrivial structural tradeoff: price differences do not change the best conductance until the bottleneck failure type switches. Unlike cactus networks the cycles overlap, so the allocation cannot decompose into independent blocks. The full-price regime keeps the expensive route positive, revealing a concrete reliability requirement. These are substantive exact design boundaries, not an arbitrary finite lookup.
